lowConfidenceBindings.instruction: Report-only per decision C. A link kind is authored in the test annotation under packages/*/test, which is outside this task's scope, so nothing was changed. Each verdict below was formed by reading the scenario in docs/specs/cognitive_line/004 (READ-ONLY) and the test body.

verdicts.heading: Should reject one Horizon transition when concurrent saves use the same expected Sequence
verdicts.link: packages/mcp-server/test/horizon-durability.test.ts :: HorizonStore: optimistic concurrency in saveTransition (kind: asserts)
verdicts.reasoning: The scenario's Given is two CONCURRENT transitions and the Then is that one persists while the stale save gets a deterministic typed conflict. The test calls saveTransition twice sequentially with the same expected Sequence 0 and asserts success then STALE_SEQUENCE. That proves the compare-and-swap REJECTS a stale expected Sequence; it does not prove that two genuinely simultaneous writers cannot both succeed, which is the read-then-write race optimistic concurrency exists to prevent and is precisely what the word 'concurrent' carries here. The test's own comment concedes the saves are sequential.
verdicts.recommendation: Downgrade to `covers-partially` with the unproven clause recorded as 'simultaneity', OR keep `asserts` only once a case drives the two saves from separate processes through ProbeHostPort.spawnWriters (003 section 5), which exists for exactly this.

verdicts.heading: Should preserve the historical scar when Recall completes
verdicts.link: packages/mcp-server/test/recall.test.ts :: Should preserve the historical scar when Recall completes (kind: asserts)
verdicts.reasoning: The Then is a conjunction: prior history AND recall provenance remain queryable, AND no admitted record is erased or directly rewritten. The test asserts only that queryRecallScar returns non-null with the expected recallId, over an InMemoryDependencyQuery with no durable rows in play. Neither 'prior history remains queryable' nor the non-erasure clause is observed. The test's own comment states the second clause is unobserved and then claims `asserts` anyway - a passing test that names the scenario's title is not the same as a test that discharges its Then.
verdicts.recommendation: Downgrade to `covers-partially`. Note the scenario already carries three other `covers-partially` links, one of them (f001-validation-audit-vulns.test.ts, completion surviving rebuildFromJsonl) closer to the non-erasure clause than this one is; a corrective pass should consider promoting THAT case rather than this one.

verdicts.heading: Should complete Relative Authority when the full lifecycle succeeds in one Horizon
verdicts.link: packages/graph-core/test/eap-lifecycle.test.ts :: 1. Should complete Relative Authority when full normative sequence succeeds in order (kind: asserts)
verdicts.confidence: lower than the other two agreements - this is the weakest of the five
verdicts.reasoning: The four ordered transitions, the `verified` state and hasRelativeAuthority() === true are all directly asserted, so the positive half of the Then is fully discharged. The restrictive half - authority 'ONLY within that Horizon' - is a negative claim and negative claims need an observed denial. hasRelativeAuthority() takes no Horizon argument and no second Horizon appears in the case, so nothing here could fail if the authority leaked. The test's comment defers that to EAP-HRZN-004 ('Should retain horizon-local authority when assignment to another Horizon is attempted'), which is a real scenario and does cover it - but one scenario's coverage does not discharge another scenario's clause.
verdicts.recommendation: Either downgrade to `covers-partially` naming the confinement clause, or - cheaper and arguably more honest - have an architect split the 'only within that Horizon' clause out of EAP-LIFE-001, since it is already registered as EAP-HRZN-004. That is a change to docs/specs/cognitive_line/004, which is frozen, so it needs an explicit decision rather than an implementer's edit.

verdicts.heading: Should exclude approval and evidence details from unauthorized projections when audit output is requested
verdicts.link: packages/mcp-server/test/f001-retry5-concurrency-authz.test.ts :: getAuditLog applies an authorization projection filter (kind: asserts)
verdicts.reasoning: The flagged concern - that 'without changing the append-only audit record' is inferred rather than asserted - does not hold on reading the test. The case runs over createEapEnv (real on-disk SQLite plus JSONL, not a double), takes a `redacted` projection as an unscoped principal, and THEN re-reads through gateway.getAuditLog as a scoped principal and asserts outcome and contractRef are still intact. That is a read-back through the store, not an inference. What it does not do is cross a restart boundary, so it proves 'unchanged' rather than 'durably unchanged'; that is a narrower gap than the one flagged.
verdicts.differentAndMoreSeriousFinding: The scenario says the host DENIES the projection. The implementation REDACTS it - returns projection: 'redacted' with executionId still present - and the test asserts redaction. Denial is only asserted for a missing principal (getAuditLog(undefined) throws). So spec and behaviour disagree about the shape of the refusal, which is a behaviour question for an architect, not a link-kind question. Raised here because it is a larger issue than the one this binding was flagged for.
verdicts.recommendation: Keep `asserts` for the projection-content clause. Route the deny-vs-redact divergence to an architect against docs/specs/cognitive_line/004 section 3.3.

verdicts.heading: Should preserve the same affected set when recall resumes from a checkpoint
verdicts.link: packages/mcp-server/test/f001-retry8-resume-index.test.ts :: re-driving a batch-cap-exhausted case finishes it and reports it as resumed (kind: asserts)
verdicts.reasoning: The flagged concern is that equality is measured against the known closure rather than against a separately executed uninterrupted run. That is the stronger oracle, not the weaker one: seedChain(s, 4) makes k1..k4 the entire closure by construction, so the expectation is independent of the code under test, whereas a second uninterrupted run shares the implementation and would agree with a wrong answer. The 'no degradation is applied twice' clause is asserted against a durable row count (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM recall_scars = 1) and the case status is read back from recall_cases, so both halves of the Then are observed.
verdicts.minorCaveat: scars.n === 1 counts scar ROWS for the tenant, not degradations per claim. If the model ever admits more than one scar row per case, that assertion stops meaning 'not applied twice'. Worth a per-claim count in a later pass; not enough to downgrade the link today.

lowConfidenceBindings.summary: 3 of 5 agreed to overclaim (EAP-PERS-004, EAP-RECL-004, EAP-LIFE-001, the last one weakly); 2 rejected on the stated reason (EAP-SEC-005, EAP-RECL-003), with one new and larger issue raised against EAP-SEC-005 (deny vs redact).

other.title: The unclaimed-test direction can only see INSIDE the declared corpus, and the corpus is declared by import
other.detail: The EAP Test Corpus is derived as every packages/*/test/**/*.test.ts that imports the Discharge Annotation surface, excluding packages/*/test/verification/** (the verification machinery's own tests, which annotate into an overridden sink). That is mechanical and drift-free for the 21 files that already annotate, but a test file covering EAP behaviour that imports no annotation surface is outside the corpus and therefore invisible to gaps.unclaimedTests. This is not hypothetical: task 06 recorded that packages/mcp-server/test/commit-atomic.test.ts and packages/mcp-server/test/tenant-isolation.test.ts cover EAP-SVCS-001/002 and EAP-PERS-003 from outside the corpus, which is why 3 of the 13 reported gaps exist. The map reports them honestly as gaps in the ANNOTATED corpus, not as gaps in the suite.
other.mitigation: corpus.undeclaredCandidates reports any non-corpus test file whose NAME matches /(^|\/)(eap-|f001-)/. It is empty today. It did not catch commit-atomic or tenant-isolation, and deliberately was not widened to: those two import nothing EAP-specific (only startServer and helpers, like every other transport test), so no mechanical signal distinguishes them and any broader rule would be a hand-list masquerading as a derivation.
other.recommendedOwner: a task-06 corrective pass - annotate those two files, which closes three gaps and brings them into the corpus by the same import rule.

other.title: The whole-suite expect() total is NOT stable run to run, which weakens one leg of task 06's no-weakening evidence
other.detail: Two consecutive full-suite runs at the same commit with no source change reported 4349 and 4360 expect() calls (877 pass, 1 todo, 0 fail, 878 tests, 141 files in both). So at least one test case issues a variable number of assertions per run. Task 06's TDD output leans on the unchanged whole-suite expect() total as the second, independent leg of its claim that annotation weakened nothing (the first being assertion-fingerprint, which covers only the 7 f001-* files and excludes matcher arguments). That leg is softer than it reads: an 11-call natural drift is larger than a single dropped assertion.
other.impact: None on this task's outputs - the Traceability Map does not read expect() counts and was byte-identical across all of these runs.
other.recommendedOwner: task 12 or task 19 (flake/fingerprint), which should either identify the varying case or stop treating the suite-wide expect() total as a fingerprint.
